chunks: Those who believe and perform good deeds will not be held guilty for what they have eaten (in the past) if they fear God and believe, and do good things and are conscious (of God) and believe, and still fear and do good, for God loves those who do good.

key_terms.اتَّقُوا: Feared God / were conscious of God

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for believers to not be guilty for what they ate in the past?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the event of the 'Abrogation of the Prohibitions,' where gradual dietary restrictions were lifted to ease the burden on the early community. The triad of 'taqwa, iman, hasanat' is interpreted not merely as a sequence but as an intensification of spiritual states, culminating in *ihsan* (excellence in worship), which aligns with the Shia emphasis on the interplay between faith and righteous action. This progression underscores that divine favor is reserved for those who continuously refine their inner consciousness alongside their outward deeds.
